tarn.name: Merian Tarn
tarn.depth_why: the shelf is 2 deep for the first cell in, 3 to the third, 4 to the fifth, 5 beyond: a tarn is a bowl, and a bowl is what makes the Lead deep enough for the open-water treasure check to pass (vanilla's needs four layers of water or air above water, ASSUMED to be Cobblemon's too: docs/world-building/ICE_LODGE.md section 5)

frost.why: white frost patches and a few blue seams in the clear ice; the ice cells that remain `minecraft:ice` are the ones the light rule protects

light_rule.why: ice melts to water on a random tick when block light at it exceeds 11 minus the light the ice filters (vanilla IceBlock; ASSUMED from the game's source, not read from the jar, so the build keeps block light at every `minecraft:ice` cell at 7 or less, one under the lowest reading); a light of level L is therefore kept at least L-7 blocks (Manhattan, walls ignored) from every ice cell

lead.why: 9 by 7 of unfrozen water (the tarn drains out under the gravel here and moving water will not freeze), fenced on the ice side with a gap on the boardwalk side. The only water in the tarn where the poke bobber's 'in_open_water' predicate can be true: every hole elsewhere is one block in a sheet of ice. The design hook for prizes (section 5 of the note) is built on that, and is NOT built.

list.why: the boardwalk from the lodge's door south along the tarn's long axis
the long spur east along the tail to shelter 3's west door
the lodge's porch deck, wider than the spine

shelter.why: a hole under a roof out of the wind, with a stool and a barrel: the one picture everyone has of ice fishing. One lantern hangs over the hole, so the hut is lit to level 11 or more at every floor cell and no monster can spawn in it. A level-15 light melts plain ice within 7 blocks (Manhattan), so every ice cell within 4 of a shelter's centre (a diamond that takes in the hut's footprint and two cells beyond each wall) is packed ice instead, which does not melt: from outside it reads as trampled white frost round the hut's door
shelter.floor_why: packed ice under the footprint and out to frost_radius; plain ice from there out is at least 8 blocks (Manhattan) from the lantern, one more than its melt reach

bunks.why: made up and slept in by nobody: SQ-MERIAN-02 'A Bed Kept Ready' (docs/story/SIDEQUESTS.md) already says the hut keeps one bunk for a traveller who stopped arriving; the quest is not built, the bunk is its place

smoke_pit.why: a ring of cobblestone with a campfire for the fish that will not dry in this air, and hay beside it

frame.why: next winter's shelter, framed in posts and rails and not yet walled

ice_stack.why: cut ice, stacked in packed ice (it keeps), with snow blocks over it: the harvest from the Lead's first holes

sled.why: a sled for the catch: slabs on runners, two barrels strapped on

keeper.name: Ketil Aune
keeper.greeting: Mind the boards. They are the only part of the tarn that is not trying to put you on your back. Ketil. I keep the holes.

topics.says: I do, every dark morning, with the long auger and a good many opinions. A hand and a thumb of ice will hold you and still let a line through. Thicker and it is a floor. Thinner is a lesson.

topics.ask: What is the open water by the post?
topics.says: The Lead. The tarn drains out under the gravel at that end, and moving water will not freeze. The little ones come to the holes. Anything that wants room goes to the Lead. I have never seen a big one at a small hole, and I have stopped taking it personally.

topics.ask: Why the huts on the ice?
topics.says: Wind. A bare hole is a hobby, a hut is a living. Three of them. Mine is the one with the good stool. Do not sit in mine.

topics.ask: Is this where the river starts?
topics.says: In the way that counts. Everything on this floor melts towards that gravel and the gravel hands it to the Tear. It comes up a good walk south and east of here as a creek you could step across, and you would never think it was this much cold. Go and look. Then come back and tell me I am wrong.

topics.ask: Can I cut my own hole?
topics.says: A pick will do it. The ice does not mind, and it skins over by morning. Keep your lantern off it, though. Light eats ice, and I would rather not start again.

topics.ask: What is the board by the door?
topics.says: The tally. I chalk the heavy ones. Nothing on it yet this winter. The fish are in a mood.

topics.ask: Why is one bunk made up?
topics.says: It is kept. Sleep in the other three.
The Warden has the Centre and the larder, and I have the water. Between us we make one competent person.
